description:
## What to remove

**`take_positive_step/2`** (`lib/enum.fz`) is a two-clause family with a `@spec` that nothing calls. `take_positive/2` inlines the same decision as an `if` inside a closure. The clause family is the shape the rest of the module uses; the closure is what actually runs.

**`Enum.slice/1`**, `fn slice(_enumerable), do: {:error, :unsupported}`, is a stray copy of the Enumerable protocol callback. That callback belongs to `Enumerable` and is implemented per type in `lib/enumerable.fz` -- List and Map answer it, Range answers it with a real slicing function. Nothing calls `Enum.slice/1`, and it occupies the name Elixir gives to `Enum.slice/2` and `Enum.slice/3`.

**`concat_list`** names two unrelated functions: `concat_list/2` appends two lists, `concat_list/1` flattens one level of a list of lists. Rename so each says what it does.

## Acceptance

- Neither dead function remains, and no caller looked for them.
- The two `concat_list` jobs have distinct names.
- Gate green. Diagnostics goldens that quote `Enum.fz` line numbers re-blessed for drift; confirm digits-stripped equality before blessing.
title: Enum: delete the dead code and the duplicate helper name
